node.title: SPI classification: high-dimensional components map to paid strata
node.statement: RESTATED (the wording correction): every rank-excess or super-slope component of the alignment incidence OUTSIDE the generic horizontal component is tangent-paid, empty, degenerate-excluded, quotient/extension-paid, or an apolar-principal scroll (the new named class: generically row-deficient pencils, ker = q_Z K(Z)[X]_{<=D-1}, priced by the R(Z) = Res(q_Z, X^n-1) dichotomy — R == 0 forces tangent payment, else O(n^2) supported slopes). The generic horizontal component is deliberately NOT claimed paid: its D_j-count is spi_point_counting (R2), a separate node.
node.notes: PROVABLE (Pro G on replay: scroll + rank-profile verticals + R(Z) dichotomy; both new lemmas verified). The wording trap caught: high dimension alone is NOT the criterion — rank-excess is. The apolar-principal scroll added as a named priceable class (taxonomy growth #3, after affine-net and dihedral). | PROVED on maintainer review of the Opus write-up (three flags recorded: R2 carve-out by design; cited inputs previously refereed; deg_Z q_Z minor-degree bound at normal-form level).
